VaR_multiplier.distinction: VaR is quantile, not tail mean

computation.ES_loss_formula: ES_loss = -mu + sigma*phi(z)/tail_prob, ES is tail mean E[L|L>VaR], strictly > VaR
computation.ES_vs_VaR_distinction: VaR_97.5% = quantile at 97.5%; ES_97.5% = mean of tail beyond VaR = sigma*phi(z)/0.025; ES_multiplier 2.3376 > VaR_multiplier 1.96, not equal

formula_basis: For L ~ N(-mu, sigma^2): VaR_alpha = -mu + sigma*Phi^-1(alpha), ES_alpha = -mu + sigma*phi(Phi^-1(alpha))/(1-alpha), where phi is standard normal pdf, Phi^-1 is quantile. ES = E[L | L > VaR]. MAR33 anchor: MAR33.2 - FRTB uses 97.5% ES replacing 99% VaR, calibrated to stressed period; parametric normal illustration uses same z_0.975=1.96 basis.
weakest_point: Assumes zero-mean normal P&L with known sigma; real P&L has fat tails, non-zero mean, heteroskedasticity; ES multiplier sensitive to phi(z) precision; using 1.96 vs 1.95996 changes ES by ~0.007%

density_phi_at_23263.note: phi(2.3263)=0.0266551 rounds to 0.02666, target 0.02665 within 1e-5 tolerance; using 2.326347874 value gives 0.02665214 = 0.02665 to 4 dec

computation.ES_vs_VaR: VaR = sigma*z = sigma*2.3263; ES = sigma*phi(z)/0.01 = sigma*2.6655; ES > VaR by factor phi(z)/(z*tail_prob) ~1.145

formula_basis: Same as case1 with alpha=0.99: VaR_0.99 = -mu + sigma*Phi^-1(0.99), ES_0.99 = -mu + sigma*phi(Phi^-1(0.99))/(0.01). MAR33 anchor: MAR33 notes 97.5% ES approximately equivalent to 99% VaR under normality; showing 99% case illustrates ES/VaR multiplier gap: VaR mult 2.3263 vs ES mult 2.6655.
weakest_point: Rounding of z to 2.3263 vs 2.326347874 creates ~300 USD difference in 1M sigma scale; density phi sensitive; normality assumption understates real tail beyond VaR

case_name: Liquidity-horizon scaled ES per MAR33 sqrt(LH/10) - Credit Spread Corporate BBB

base_ES_10d.source: Case1 precise ES 97.5% for sigma 1M, 10-day base horizon

inputs.risk_factor_category: Credit spread - investment grade BBB (per MAR33.12)

computation.MAR33_aggregation_note: In full MAR33, total ES = sqrt( sum_j ES_j^2 ) across 5 LH categories with sqrt scaling per category; this case shows single category scaling

formula_basis: MAR33.12-MAR33.16: Liquidity horizons LH = 10,20,40,60,120 days by risk factor category (e.g., IR large cap 10d, credit IG BBB 40d, equity small cap 20d, commodity 60d, vol 120d). Scaled ES: ES_j(LH) = ES_j(10d)*sqrt(LH/10). For LH=40, factor = sqrt(4)=2. Symbolic: ES_LH = ES_10 * (LH/10)^0.5
weakest_point: Assumes independent increments and sqrt-time scaling holds; real liquidity horizons have overlap and correlation; using single ES_10 as base ignores stressed calibration and aggregation across categories; sqrt scaling is MAR33 simplification, not true market diffusion

PnL_sample_20.note: Unsorted as supplied; P&L negative = loss

computation.tail_selection_rule_explicit: At 97.5% with N=20, tail contains 0.5 observations on average. MAR33 text does not prescribe fractional observation treatment for HS ES in small samples. Must choose convention honestly.
computation.convention_chosen: Conservative ceil convention: ES_HS = mean of worst ceil((1-alpha)*N) = mean of worst 1 observation. Alternative fractional-weighted convention: weight = 0.5 observation. Both named as conventions where regulatory text is silent.

fractional_weighted_method.description: Weighted ES = (0.5 * worst) / 0.5 = worst = -5.2M; if using linear interpolation between worst and second worst for VaR, VaR would be between -5.2 and -3.8

VaR_interpolated_example.method: VaR as worst if ceil, or -4.5 if average of worst 2? Common HS VaR 97.5% with 20 obs uses 1st worst = -5.2

ES_HS_PnL_mean_worst2_illustrative.note: If convention used ceil to 2 for conservatism

computation.VaR_vs_ES_distinction_HS: VaR_HS_97.5% = quantile threshold (approx -5.2M P&L with ceil); ES_HS_97.5% = average of P&L <= VaR threshold = -5.2M in ceil1 convention; ES is tail mean, not just quantile

formula_basis: Historical Simulation ES: Order P&L ascending: P&L_(1) <=... <= P&L_(N). For confidence alpha, k = (1-alpha)*N. VaR_HS = -quantile = -P&L_(floor(k)) or interpolated. ES_HS = (1/k')* sum_{i=1}^{k'} P&L_(i) for P&L_(i) <= VaR threshold, where k' = number of observations in tail. For N=20, alpha=0.975, k=0.5. MAR33 anchor: MAR33.12-MAR33.18 HS ES definition: ES = average of losses exceeding VaR; tail selection requires handling fractional observations. Symbolic: ES_alpha = (1/|Tail|)* sum_{L_i > VaR_alpha} L_i
weakest_point: N=20 gives only 0.5 expected exceedances at 97.5%, so ES estimate has huge sampling error and depends critically on fractional treatment convention (ceil vs interpolation vs weighting) which MAR33 does not prescribe for tiny samples; with 1 observation, ES = VaR, losing ES vs VaR distinction benefit; real FRTB requires 250+ days and stressed period
